neighbours.label: clause-linking word that opens a consequence or reason clause after a complete statement (', making', 'because', 'so much that', ', where')
fire: Most of the seeds sprouted within a week, making the garden look green by early May.
The bridge was closed for repairs, forcing commuters to take the long ferry instead.
The museum stayed open late on Fridays because the new director wanted to attract students.
The vines grew so thick that they covered almost the entire south wall of the barn.
The old recipe uses very little sugar, which makes the pie taste sharp and tart.
Many families moved north in the 1950s, where factory jobs paid far better wages.
The river flooded every spring, so farmers learned to plant only after the water fell.
The lake froze solid early that winter, allowing villagers to walk across to the island.
